The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has released the names of 85 beneficiaries of his domestic postgraduate scholarship programme, who will pursue various Master’s degree programmes at Bayero University, Kano. Barau announced this in a Facebook post on Friday, saying he would present admission letters to the beneficiaries on Monday, November 9, 2026. The beneficiaries, selected through the Barau I. Jibrin Foundation, will study courses including Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Climate Change, Natural Resource Management, Computer Science, Civil Engineering and Solar Energy Technology, among others. Explaining the rationale behind the initiative, Barau said the programme was part of his sustained commitment to developing human capital and advancing Kano State and Nigeria. He said, “Hundreds of indigent students have benefited from both my domestic and foreign scholarship programmes as part of our sustained commitment to human capital development and the advancement of Kano State and Nigeria at large. Announcing the presentation of admission letters, Barau said, “By the grace of Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta’ala, I will, on Monday, November 9, 2026, present admission letters to beneficiaries of my Domestic Postgraduate Scholarship Programme in Kano.” He explained that the successful applicants had been selected to pursue Master’s degrees in several specialised fields at Bayero University, Kano. “Through my foundation, the Barau I. Jibrin Foundation (BIJF), the beneficiaries have been carefully selected to pursue Master of Science (MSc) degrees in various cutting-edge fields, including Cybersecurity, Solar Energy Technology, Software Engineering, Climate Change, Information Technology, and Natural Resources Management, among others, at Bayero University, Kano (BUK),” he said. Congratulating the beneficiaries, the senator wished them success in their academic pursuits. “Congratulations to all the successful applicants.
